title: Frequency of Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with polyuria (dilute urine), polydipsia (excessive thirst), nocturia, and hypernatremia. Central DI: deficiency of ADH (vasopressin) from posterior pituitary → inability to concentrate urine. Nephrogenic DI: kidneys resistant to ADH (lithium, hypercalcemia, hypokalemia). Workup: 24h urine volume (>3L/day), urine osmolality (<300 despite hypernatremia), serum osmolality elevated, hypernatremia. Water deprivation test: cannot concentrate urine despite fluid restriction. After desmopressin (DDAVP): central DI = urine osmolality increases >50% (kidneys respond to exogenous ADH). Nephrogenic DI = no response. Treatment: central DI → desmopressin (DDAVP) intranasal or PO. Nephrogenic → treat underlying cause, thiazide diuretics (paradoxically reduce urine output), low-solute diet. Free water access essential.

stacks.label: 24h urine volume / Serum & urine osmolality
stacks.finding: Dilute urine <300, high serum osmo, hyperNa.

stacks.label: Water deprivation test + DDAVP
stacks.finding: Central DI: responds to DDAVP (>50% rise in Uosm).
